newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgium moves troops to Zambia for Zaire evacuation.
newsitem.headline: Belgium moves troops to Zambia for Zaire evacuation.

text.p: Belgium on Saturday moved 18 of its 550-strong paratroop force stationed in Congo to the Zambian copperbelt town of Ndola, south of Zaire's second city Lubumbashi, which is expected to fall to rebel forces before long.

"In the framework of its mission, the Belgian detachment at Brazzaville will send a reconnaissance team to Ndola in Zambia. Its aim is to prepare the eventual evacuation of our nationals in Lubumbashi," the Belgian army press office said in a statement.
An additional five soldiers would also be stationed at the Belgian consulate in Lubumbashi to improve security, it said.

Estimates of the number of Belgians in Lubumbashi, the centre of Zaire's mineral-rich Shaba province, range from 500 to 1,500. So far the Belgians, many of whom work in the copper mining industry, have ignored countless requests from the foreign ministry to leave the country.

The Belgian troops in Congo are stationed alongside U.S., French and British forces ready to evacuate their nationals from Zaire's capital Kinshasa, across the Congo river from Brazzaville, should peace talks that began today in South Africa fail to halt the country's civil war.
